analysis.title: Nasdaq Futures: Is Length Still Elevated?
key_insights: Despite price turbulence over October 13th-20th, Nasdaq Non-Dealer net positioning reached a new nominal high per Commitment of Traders. Non-Dealers bought $9.5bn as the index lost 3.5%.
That was the 3rd straight week of Non-Dealer buying, for a cumulative $21.8bn since September 29th.

On October 22nd Meta fell 7.0% after its earnings and led a broad decline in AI-related exposure: HyperScalers -4.1%, Memory -8.6%, Semiconductors -6.5%. Meta forecast significant spending increases, which rattled credit markets already concerned about the sustainability of the debt-fueled AI infrastructure boom.
On October 22nd Nasdaq fell 2.9% and futures aggregate open interest rose $10.6bn, the largest 1-day jump in 2026 excluding roll periods. Funding underperformed, so sizeable shorts were initiated.

During October 22nd-26th Nasdaq recouped 1.1% and futures open interest retraced $9bn. Tactical downside shorts were unwound, and longs were also cut as funding cheapened on an outright and relative basis.
CTAs were likely a key driver of the long liquidation, given a momentum break on the GS Futures Strategists' framework.
Length remains elevated heading into more MegaCap tech results. If Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet fail to impress, meaningful futures selling could follow.
earnings_insights: Meta (reported around 10/22): shares fell 7.0% on 10/22 after the company forecast significant spending increases. No EPS or revenue figures are given in the note.
Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet results are upcoming. GS says a failure to impress could bring meaningful Nasdaq futures selling.
risk_factors: Weak results from Amazon, Microsoft or Alphabet could trigger meaningful Nasdaq futures selling while length is still elevated.
Credit markets are concerned about the sustainability of the debt-fueled AI infrastructure boom, and Meta's higher spending forecast aggravated that concern.
CTA momentum break could add systematic selling.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq Non-Dealer net futures positioning hit a new nominal high per CFTC Commitment of Traders data as of October 20th.
Non-Dealers bought $9.5bn in the week of Oct 13-20 while the index fell 3.5%, the 3rd straight week of buying and $21.8bn cumulative since September 29th.
Nasdaq futures aggregate open interest rose $10.6bn on October 22nd, the largest 1-day jump in 2026 excluding roll periods, then retraced $9bn over October 22nd-26th.
Nasdaq futures funding underperformed on October 22nd and cheapened outright and relative to other measures by October 26th, which contributed to longs being cut.
CTAs likely drove selling after a momentum break on the GS Futures Strategists' Nasdaq CTA momentum thresholds.
